item.research_question: Can a novel hybrid-rolling process combining cryo-rolling and warm-rolling create a dual structural-compositional heterogeneous microstructure in an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to achieve unprecedented strength-ductility synergy?
item.processing_route: Hybrid-rolling consisting of two stages: Stage I cryo-rolling to a true strain of ~1.2 (90% reduction in thickness total) with samples immersed in liquid N2 for 30 minutes before and after each pass; Stage II warm-rolling at 600 °C to a true strain of ~1.2, with specimens held at 600 °C for 20 minutes prior to each of the ten passes and water quenched immediately after every pass.
item.test_conditions: Tensile tests performed along the rolling direction (RD) at ambient temperature using a universal testing machine with an initial strain rate of 8.3 × 10−4 s−1.
key_findings: The hybrid-rolled EHEA achieved a yield strength (σYS) of ~1900 MPa and ultimate tensile strength (σUTS) of ~2000 MPa.
The hybrid-rolled EHEA maintained an elongation to failure (ef) of ~8%, which is more than twice that of the cryo-rolled material (~3%).
The specific strength of the hybrid-rolled EHEA was ~270 kNm.kg−1, at least 50% higher than commercial alloys like Ti-6Al-4V with similar elongation.
The microstructure consisted of retained lamellar regions (LRs) and adjacent nearly equiaxed nanocrystalline regions (NCRs) with an average grain size of ~240 nm.
The NCRs exhibited compositional heterogeneity with four distinct phases: L12 (NCR-1), disordered FCC (NCR-2), B2 (NCR-3), and Cr-rich B2 (NCR-4).
Approximately 70% of the grains in the NCRs were in a deformed state (KAM ≥ 1°), while ~30% were recrystallized.
The volume fractions of FCC and B2 phases in the as-cast condition were ~65% and 35%, respectively, with lamellae thicknesses of ~640 ± 40 nm and 240 ± 15 nm.
item.mechanism: The extreme heterogeneities result from stored energy in cryo-rolled broken lamellar regions (BLRs) accelerating transformations during warm-rolling, creating dual structural (LRs vs NCRs) and compositional (different phases) heterogeneities. Mechanical incompatibility between domains with different hardness generates strain gradients accommodated by geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs), leading to long-range back stress that prevents early necking and enhances both strength and ductility.
item.limitations: The authors state that the quantification of the back stress and its enhancement through further microstructural tuning remains a topic for future work.
item.future_work: The authors propose to evaluate the quantification of the back stress and its enhancement through further microstructural tuning in hybrid-processed dual structural-compositional heterogeneous EHEA.
quotes: The novel processing strategy resulted in an extremely heterogeneous microstructure consisting of retained lamellar and transformed nanocrystalline regions.
The dual heterogeneous microstructure yielded an unprecedented combination of strength (~2000 MPa) and ductility (~8%).
The massive back-stress strengthening in such heterogeneous microstructural arrangements results in super-strong EHEA coupled with appreciable ductility.
